opening: Covering a grid completely with dominoes, and counting the ways.

steps.prompt: In how many ways can a 2 by 3 grid be covered with dominoes (1 by 2 tiles, placed either way)?
nudges: What can cover the leftmost column?
Can the first column be covered by vertical dominoes only?

steps.prompt: The grid is filled column by column, left to right. When column $j$ has just been completed, what do you need to know to continue?
options: Which cells of column $j + 1$ are already covered by dominoes sticking out of column $j$
How every earlier column was covered
How many dominoes have been used
nudges: Which earlier dominoes can still interfere with later columns?
steps.showed: Only the horizontal dominoes that start in column $j$ reach further, and they reach exactly one column. That pattern of covered cells is a mask.

steps.prompt: The task has $n \le 10$ rows and $m \le 1000$ columns. With the mask running along a column, how many different masks are there at most?
nudges: How many bits does a mask have, one per row?
steps.showed: A thousand masks times a thousand columns: a million states.

steps.prompt: Why does the mask run along the side of length 10 and not along the side of length 1000?
options: The number of masks is 2 to the power of that side
nudges: How many masks would a side of 1000 give?
steps.showed: The exponential part must sit on the short side. If the input can come either way round, swap it.

steps.prompt: In how many ways can a 4 by 7 grid be covered?
nudges: From one mask, which masks of the next column can follow?
steps.showed: For each mask, fill the free cells of the column with vertical dominoes or with horizontal ones that mark the next column.

steps.prompt: In how many ways can a 5 by 7 grid be covered?
nudges: How many cells does the grid have?
steps.showed: None: 35 cells cannot be split into pairs. A good first test for any tiling program.

steps.prompt: In how many ways can a 6 by 6 grid be covered?
nudges: Would the direct search over the whole grid still be feasible at 10 by 1000?
steps.showed: The column-by-column table gets there with 64 masks and 6 columns.

reveal.name: A profile of what sticks out
reveal.statement: Go through the grid column by column. The only memory needed is which cells of the next column are already covered by tiles sticking out of this one: a mask.
reveal.remark: The mask runs along the short side.
